entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adeimantus of Corinth was a Corinthian commander who played a pivotal role in the invasion of Greece by Xerxes.


As the son of Ocytus, Adeimantus was groomed for leadership and led the Corinthian forces during the invasion.


Before the Battle of Artemisium, Adeimantus threatened to sail away, demonstrating his willingness to challenge Xerxes' authority.









Adeimantus' actions had significant consequences, including the failure of the Corinthian forces and the eventual retreat of the Greek army.









The legacy of Adeimantus can be seen in the eventual defeat of Xerxes' forces and the preservation of Greek independence.









Adeimantus' story serves as a reminder of the importance of leadership and strategic decision-making in the face of overwhelming odds.









In the annals of history, Adeimantus of Corinth stands as a testament to the bravery and cunning of a lesser-known hero.
